title: Nok culture terracottas and early iron metallurgy
summary: The Nok culture of central Nigeria is known for fired-clay sculptures and for iron-smelting furnaces. Sources place the culture from perhaps 900 BCE to about 200 CE, with dated terracottas and furnaces clustering near 500 BCE. A Goethe University Frankfurt team now excavates in the region, where looting has damaged many sites.

uncertainty.note: Start is c. 500 BCE, when dated terracottas and smelting furnaces cluster; the culture itself may begin c. 900-1000 BCE. End is c. 200 CE in one source, c. 500 CE in another.

as_recorded.value: existing from at least 900 B.C. to about A.D. 200

when.display: c. 500 BCE-200 CE (culture possibly from c. 900 BCE)

where.modern_name: Nok culture area, central Nigeria (pin is the Jos Plateau)
where.historical_name: Nok culture area, central Nigeria; no polity names are known

importance.justification: One of the earliest known sculptural and iron-working cultures in sub-Saharan Africa.

sources.title: Wikidata item Q811142 (Jos Plateau), coordinate location (P625)

reviewer_note: Dates differ between sources (900 vs 1000 BCE start; 200 vs 500 CE end). The Goethe University Frankfurt iron-furnace dissertation (27 furnaces, middle of first millennium BCE) appeared only in search snippets and its page was blocked, so its figures are not used. Pin is the broad Jos Plateau region, not a single site.
